title: Toshiro Mifune's birth chart
metaDescription: Toshiro Mifune's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 11.1° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 11.1° Aries, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 11.1° Aries. That falls in the second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by the Sun in the classical scheme — a fire sign read through a cardinal season.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 21.8° Pisces, Venus was at 16.6° Pisces, Mars was at 7.3° Scorpio. Read together: a mind that absorbs before it argues; taste tuned to mood and undertow; drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Saturn and Pluto hold the closest angle here — a sextile, 0.2° wide. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, Jupiter conjunction Neptune at 0.7°, and Mars square Jupiter at 0.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Mars, Uranus, Pluto close a triangle of trines. A grand trine is read as self-sufficiency in one element: the current circulates whether or not anything is asked of it.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has four entries for this chart. The Sun in Aries at 11.1° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mercury in Pisces at 21.8° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Pisces at 16.6° is in exaltation; Mars in Scorpio at 7.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives water 5, fire 3, earth 2, and mutable 5, fixed 3, cardinal 2 across the modes. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn and Neptune were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Virgo for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.3° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 13.5°.
